title: Automated device cleanup: device threshold, inactive removal, permanent deletion

prose.text: Three tenant-wide settings remove and delete device records without an admin acting on each one. They change records in the portal only.

prose.label: Inactive removal.
prose.text: {{inactive-removal}} Which timestamp marks a device inactive is stated two ways {{divergence:inactivity-timestamp}}.

prose.label: Permanent deletion.
prose.text: {{permanent-delete}} {{delete-from-unregistered-and-removed}} The Terraform provider accepts deletion periods the console does not offer {{divergence:purge-period-values}}.

prose.label: Timing.
prose.text: {{week-lag}} Cleanup removes records, not the app: [[zcc.devices.lifecycle:removal-not-uninstall]].

prose.label: API.
prose.text: {{api-fields-untyped}} The Terraform provider labels some values, but which API field holds which console setting, and what most force-remove type codes mean, is only partly known {{gap:field-to-setting-mapping}}.

checks.do: Whether a device the user did not remove was taken by the threshold (the user enrolled a newer device past it) or by inactivity, from its state history and the cleanup settings.
Whether a cleanup setting was changed within the last week, since the Enrolled Devices view can lag that long.

threshold.statement: Force Remove Oldest Device After User Enrolls sets a threshold number of devices; when a user enrolls a device past it, Client Connector force removes the user's oldest device. The default, Restrict, removes nothing, and an error is shown when a user tries to enroll more than 16 devices.

quotes: If a user attempts to enroll a device after reaching the threshold number, Zscaler Client Connector force removes the oldest device.
The default setting is Restrict, which means no devices are removed. An error is displayed when a user tries to enroll more than 16 devices.

threshold-minimum.statement: Lowering the minimum threshold to one device requires contacting the vendor.

quotes: Contact Zscaler Client Connector to change the minimum threshold to 1 device.

inactive-removal.statement: Automatically Force Remove Inactive Devices After removes a device that has not connected to Internet & SaaS within the chosen period: 30, 60, 90, 120, 150 or 180 days, or Never, which is the default.

quotes: Zscaler Client Connector automatically removes a device if it doesn't connect to Internet & SaaS in the defined period and becomes inactive.
Select from the following intervals: 30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180 days, or Never. The default setting is Never.

permanent-delete.statement: Permanently Delete Removed Devices After deletes a device from the admin console after it has been Removed or Unregistered for 60, 90, 120, 150 or 180 days, measured from the device's Last Deregistration Timestamp.

quotes: Select the period after which a device is permanently removed from the Zscaler Admin Console after being in the Removed or Unregistered state.
Select from the following intervals: 60, 90, 120, 150, or 180 days.
Zscaler Client Connector uses the device’s Last Deregistration Timestamp to determine how long the device was in the Removed or Unregistered state

delete-from-unregistered-and-removed.statement: The device-states table applies the same permanent deletion to devices in the Unregistered state and in the Removed state.

quotes: The device is permanently removed from the Zscaler Admin Console when it's been in the Unregistered state for the time configured
The device is permanently removed from the Zscaler Admin Console when it's been in Removed state for the time configured

week-lag.statement: After cleanup settings change, Enrolled Devices can take up to a week to reflect it.

quotes: After modifying settings, it can take up to a week for Enrolled Devices to reflect changes.

api-fields-untyped.statement: The API contract for reading and writing cleanup (`getDeviceCleanupInfo`, `setDeviceCleanupInfo`) types every field as a string, including `active`, `autoRemovalDays`, `autoPurgeDays`, `deviceExceedLimit` and `forceRemoveType`, with no descriptions, defaults or allowed values.

inactivity-timestamp.summary: Which timestamp decides that a device is inactive for automatic removal.

quotes: A device becomes inactive when the most recent KeepAlive Timestamp is older than the defined period.

positions.says: The device's most recent KeepAlive Timestamp.

quotes: An inactive device is based on the Last Seen Connected to ZIA timestamp associated with the Zscaler Client Connector registration.

positions.says: The device's Last Seen Connected to ZIA timestamp.

inactivity-timestamp.impact: A device that keeps sending keepalives but never connects to Internet & SaaS (for example a ZPA-only user) is kept by one reading and removed by the other, so predicting which devices cleanup will take needs the right timestamp.

purge-period-values.summary: Which permanent-deletion periods can be set.

quotes: Select from the following intervals: 60, 90, 120, 150, or 180 days.

positions.says: The console offers 60, 90, 120, 150 or 180 days, with no 0, 30 or Never.
The ZCC Terraform provider's `auto_purge_days` also accepts 0 and 30.

quotes: \ \"autoPurgeDays\" : \"0\"\n}"

positions.says: A recorded cleanup read from one test tenant (recorded with SDK 1.9.13, Python SDK cassette) carries `autoPurgeDays` "0", a value the console does not list.

purge-period-values.impact: A Terraform plan with `auto_purge_days` of 30 passes the provider's validation for a period the console does not offer, so the API may reject it or store a value the console cannot show; and a tenant reading 0 cannot tell from the console what deletion period, if any, is in force.

field-to-setting-mapping.title: Which cleanup API field holds which console setting, and their value encodings
field-to-setting-mapping.detail: Unverified legacy statement: `autoRemovalDays` is the inactive-removal period (0 or null for Never), `autoPurgeDays` the permanent-deletion period, `deviceExceedLimit` the per-user threshold (1 to 16), and `forceRemoveType` an integer enum of the force-remove type with `forceRemoveTypeString` its display form. The contract gives only names and string types and the SDKs carry the fields without describing them, but the ZCC Terraform provider's `zcc_device_cleanup` resource describes and validates them (generated surface): `auto_removal_days` takes 0 (Never), 30, 60, 90, 120, 150 or 180; `auto_purge_days` takes 0, 30, 60, 90, 120, 150 or 180 with no label for 0 (divergence purge-period-values); `force_remove_type` takes 0 (Restrict) or 8 through 16, and the codes 8 to 16 have no labels. A recorded `getDeviceCleanupInfo` response from one test tenant (recorded with SDK 1.9.13, Python SDK cassette) sends the values as strings: `forceRemoveType` "0", `deviceExceedLimit` "16", `autoRemovalDays` "0", `autoPurgeDays` "0". What the force-remove codes 8 to 16 mean, and how `deviceExceedLimit` relates to them, is still open.
